module_role: MODBUS application-layer server (and/or client) module — implements the function-code processor + ADU framer/parser for one or more of the three published transports (RTU, ASCII, TCP). On the host-side it exposes the four data tables (Discrete Inputs, Coils, Input Registers, Holding Registers) plus diagnostic counters and an optional Encapsulated Interface (FC 0x2B) handler.
top_module: modbus_server_top (or modbus_client_top, or modbus_gateway_top for bridges); naming is vendor-specific.

integration_overview.host_side: Two memory-mapped regions: (a) configuration / control / status registers (server address, mode, baud, MBAP_unit_id, comm-event counters), (b) the four MODBUS data tables (Discrete Inputs, Coils, Input Registers, Holding Registers) backed by RAM or by application-supplied read/write callbacks.
integration_overview.wire_side_rtu: UART TX / RX pair plus optional RTS for RS-485 transceiver direction control. T3.5 silence timer is internal.
integration_overview.wire_side_ascii: UART TX / RX pair; LRC / CR LF detection internal.
integration_overview.wire_side_tcp: TCP socket on port 502 — typically delegated to an external TCP/IP stack (lwIP, FreeRTOS+TCP, etc.).
integration_overview.clock_source: Implementation-defined — typically a single system clock that drives the UART baud generator (RTU/ASCII) or the Ethernet MAC reference (TCP).
integration_overview.reset_source: Implementation-defined — usually a synchronous reset that clears the diagnostic counters and re-initializes the framer state.
integration_overview.interrupt_routing: End-of-frame on UART RX (T3.5 silence expiration or CR LF detection); TCP segment received; response-transmit-complete; framing-error detected.

interface_categories: Host CPU bus (APB / AHB / AXI / Avalon / Wishbone — vendor choice) for register / data-table access
Serial UART pair (TX, RX, optional RTS for RS-485 direction) for RTU and ASCII
TCP socket (delegated to a TCP/IP stack) for Modbus TCP
Diagnostic counter readout interface (mapped through FC 0x08 or via local CPU register window)
Optional File Record store (FC 20 / 21) — flash / EEPROM region
Optional FIFO queue (FC 24) — application-defined FIFO buffer
interconnect_topologies_supported: Modbus RTU multi-drop bus on EIA/TIA-485 — single client + up to 247 individual servers (address 1..247); address 0 broadcast.
Modbus RTU point-to-point on EIA/TIA-232 — single client + single server.
Modbus ASCII multi-drop / point-to-point on the same physical layers as RTU.

Modbus TCP — switched-Ethernet client/server; multiple concurrent clients per server are supported (the server demultiplexes by TCP connection; Transaction ID disambiguates pipelined requests on each connection).
Modbus gateway — bridges a TCP front-end to one or more serial sub-networks; MBAP.Unit_ID selects which downstream serial address to forward to.
Modbus PLUS (MB+) — legacy HDLC-based token-passing peer-to-peer network (Modicon-proprietary).
default_signal_values_when_omitted: Diagnostic counters and Comm Event Counter / Log reset to zero on power-up. Data tables hold application-defined defaults. Run Indicator Status defaults to 0xFF (running) once the server's main loop is dispatched.
soc_dependent_items: Baud rate, parity, stop-bit configuration for serial transports
Sizing of the four data tables (number of coils, registers, etc.) and their backing-RAM allocation
File-record subsystem presence (FC 20 / 21) and its flash / EEPROM mapping
Diagnostic counter persistence across reset (volatile vs non-volatile)
Sub-function set supported under FC 0x08 (subset of 0..18, 20)
Encapsulated Interface support (FC 0x2B): CANopen General Reference (MEI 13) and/or Read Device Identification (MEI 14) and the device-identification object set populated
Gateway routing table (if implementing a gateway)
Listen-Only Mode escape mechanism (only sub-function 0x0001 Restart Communications Option can exit it per spec)

low_power_modes.n_a_at_protocol_layer: MODBUS does not define low-power states; any implementation is free to gate clocks / sleep the host CPU between transactions.

compatibility_notes: All three transports carry the same PDU; an application written against the function-code set is portable across RTU / ASCII / TCP modulo transport-only function codes (FC 7, 8, 11, 12, 17 are serial-only).
MBAP.Protocol_ID is always 0x0000 for MODBUS; non-zero values are reserved for future use and shall be rejected.

Function-code-43 / MEI-13 (CANopen General Reference) requires consulting CiA documentation for the encapsulated payload format; MEI-14 (Read Device Identification) is fully defined in section 6.21 of this spec.
Reserved function codes (Annex A) shall not be implemented by interoperable devices: FC 8/19, 8/21-65535, 9, 10, 13, 14, 41, 42, 90, 91, 125, 126, 127, and FC 43 sub-MEI 0..12 and 15..255.
Modbus PLUS uses the same function-code set but is Modicon-proprietary; not covered in detail in this version-1.1b3 application protocol document.

Some vendors implement 32-bit float / 32-bit integer across two consecutive holding registers; the spec defines only 16-bit registers, so any 32-bit encoding (big-/little-/mixed-endian word order) is a vendor convention and must be documented at the application level.
